wishes: Announce 'Tonight: <film>' in a live region after a spin and move focus to the result
A text-only recipe view with headings per dish and quantities in each step
Tagged or text PDF, or a plain 'email me the shopping list' option
Skip link to the menu
loved: Welcome dialog is a real modal with focus trapped and a sensible first focus
Find a film suggestions are real buttons, very quick to use
Prep sheet has proper headings for each aisle (Meat, Produce, Dairy) so the shopping list is easy to move through
Add buttons in Goes well with have clear labels like 'Add Coconut ice'
Mark as watched button names the film
quote: The bones are better than most sites. Search, the prep sheet headings and labelled buttons all work. But I spun the wheel and my phone went silent, so I had no idea what film I'd landed on.
would_pay: no, not until spin results are announced and recipes read properly; maybe a few dollars after that

frictions.evidence: P33-02-homefull.png

frictions.what: Six typefaces (Oswald, Jost, Limelight, IBM Plex Sans Condensed, Aldrich, Cedarville Cursive) plus menu fonts, and three separate visual worlds (deco cinema, 90s video store, candy counter). Each is lovely on its own but the switch is jarring

frictions.evidence: s3.py: 3.0 s to the menu; mobile with reduced_motion still curtained at 9 s (P16-04-mobile-menu.png)

frictions.what: Menu of the week (Lady and the Tramp) sits above the wheel and competes with the main job of the page

wishes: Scroll to the section, or collapse the hero, when a top tab is tapped
Start on an empty state, not a pre-loaded Ghostbusters
One shared type scale and button system across the three sections
Respect prefers-reduced-motion and make the curtain skippable
loved: The printed menus are the star. Each film gets its own layout (Jaws ship's mess ration card, Us funhouse snack bar, Hobbit recipe box) and they look like real props
The marquee showing the picked film's title is a great touch
Vegetarian mode really rewrites dishes (mushroom 'calamari', hearts of palm lobster rolls, soy instead of Worcestershire, vegetarian parmesan-style cheese) instead of just dropping meat
The video store tape cards with the trailer TV and rating sticker are beautifully done
Contrast is mostly fine; only small uppercase labels at 11.5px
quote: This is the most fun I've seen in a recipe app, the menus feel like real props. It just needs to stop opening on a ghost Ghostbusters and to show me something when I tap a tab.
would_pay: maybe, $5 to 10 one-off for printable menu packs or a party kit; not a subscription

wishes: One clear first step: no film pre-selected, a big Spin, and everything else hangs off the chosen film
Send shopping list to Reminders, Notes or a supermarket app
Rough cost per head
Proper About and privacy page before any sync feature ships
Double feature that starts from the current film
A4 PDF with real text
loved: Fast: first paint about 0.5 s on phone, about 1.1 MB transferred
Each film menu is unique and themed, which is the real moat
Guest scaling from 1 to 24 and make-ahead notes are genuinely useful
Streaming info for Australian services (Binge, Stan, Foxtel Now, SBS, ABC iview)
Video store seasonal aisles (Halloween, Melbourne Cup, Christmas countdown) give a reason to come back
Saved menus and lock-in survive a reload
quote: The content is the product here, 850 bespoke menus is a lot of work and it shows. What's missing is the boring stuff: a clear first step, a privacy page and a way to get the shopping list onto my phone.
would_pay: maybe: $4 to 6 one-off or about $15 a year for sync, holiday party packs and shopping list export; would not pay for the core spin

frictions.evidence: 'Saved on this device. Reset clears stubs, saved menus, watched films, this week's film, rentals and settings.'

frictions.what: Page loads fonts from Google and posters from TMDB on every visit, and trailers from YouTube; this isn't mentioned
frictions.evidence: pr.py hosts: fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com, image.tmdb.org; youtube-nocookie embed in source

frictions.what: Member card is created on first visit (number and 'member since' date) without asking
frictions.evidence: mns-member={no:337262, since:..., name:'', rentals:0} after one spin

wishes: A short plain 'What we keep' panel: on this device, what goes online only if you turn on card sync, nothing else
Delete my online card button
Longer PIN or a magic link
Say up front there's no account, no tracking, no ads
loved: No cookies, no analytics, no ad trackers at all
Everything is kept on the device by default and Reset everything clears it
Share link only carries the film name (?film=...), nothing personal
Reset options are split (stubs, saved menus, everything)
quote: It's actually very tidy, nothing is tracked and it all stays on my computer. But the minute it offers to put my card online with a four digit PIN, I want to know where it's going, and nothing tells me.
would_pay: no for the app itself; maybe a small amount for sync if it explained where data lives and let me delete it

Real quotes, or mark the invented ones as house notes

loved: Release years were right on all 49 I checked
Star Wars in release order includes Rogue One and Solo in the right spots; Middle-earth runs Rings then Hobbits by release
Mad Max 2 under its proper Australian title, and Furiosa included
Godfather, Back to the Future, Indiana Jones, Lethal Weapon, Harry Potter, Toy Story and the Dark Knight runs are complete
Marathon menu logic (snack and drink per film, mains first and last, dessert at halfway) is clever, and you can untick films
quote: The years are spot on and the marathon menu idea is a beauty. But don't tell me Alien is part 1 of 2, and you can't go from Rocky IV straight to Creed.
would_pay: no; maybe $5 if the series were complete and the marathons had running times

wishes: Per-dish recipe card: ingredients with amounts, then steps with amounts inline
Separate hands-on time from waiting time
Scale the method text (number of rissoles, tins, batches), not just the list
Merge the same ingredient across dishes (one rice, one passata)
Oven temps for every bake and fry, including chip first-fry
loved: Methods read like a real cook wrote them: 185C for squid, 170C for arancini, 240C then 160C for crackling, salt the pork skin and dry it overnight
Make-ahead notes are genuinely useful for a dinner party
Proper Aussie ingredients: tasty cheese, thickened cream, cornflour sponge, kabana and pickled onions for The Castle
Timpano for Big Night shows someone knows the film
Vegetarian swaps are sensible, not lazy
quote: Whoever wrote these methods can cook, the temperatures are right and the make-ahead notes are gold. But give me an ingredient list per dish, and don't tell me chilling a can of Coke is four hours of cooking.
would_pay: maybe: $5 to 10 for proper per-dish recipe cards and a reliable scaler for a big family; not for the current format
